name: Employees Provident Fund

references.title: Employees Provident Fund Act 1991 (Act 452)
references.locator: s.43 and Third Schedule Parts A and E
references.quote: Part A: Malaysian citizens, permanent residents and pre-1-August-1998 electors below 60; Part E: Malaysian citizens aged 60 and above (Part E by its own terms reaches Malaysian citizens only). A non-citizen contributes under Part F; a permanent resident or pre-1998 elector aged 60 or above contributes under Part C. The first printed row of both Parts is NIL: wages of RM0.01 to RM10.00 attract no contribution. Above the table the total contribution is rounded up to the next ringgit and the employer’s share is that total less the employee’s rounded share, never two separate round-ups. Bands: RM20 to RM5,000, RM100 to RM20,000, contribution taken on the band's upper limit; employee 11%, employer 13% up to RM5,000 and 12% above; above RM20,000 each share is its percentage of the wage; Part E is the employer's 4% alone. Part A note under the RM5,000 row: "Where the employer pays bonus to an employee who receives monthly wages of RM5,000.00 and below, and upon receiving the said bonus renders the wages received for that month to exceed RM5,000.00, the employer’s contribution shall be calculated at the rate of 13% of the amount of wages for the month. The total contribution which includes cents shall be rounded to the next ringgit." The employee's share stays on the printed row. The Act does not state how the total splits between the two shares above RM20,000. Part A para 1(c) and Part C para 1(c): a non-citizen who elected to contribute before 1 August 1998 stays on Part A below 60 and Part C from 60. The same bonus note covers those electors.

references.title: Employees Provident Fund Act 1991 (Act 452)
references.locator: s.2 "wages"; s.48(1)-(2); s.51(2B)(a); First Schedule paras (2)-(3), (8), (13)
references.quote: "Wages" excludes a retrenchment, lay-off or termination benefit, a payment in lieu of notice and "overtime payment". A person who has attained seventy-five is not an employee (First Schedule para (13)) and s.51(2B)(a) credits nothing to a member after seventy-five, so no part of the Third Schedule is charged after the month the person turns 75: the Act and KWSP set no rule for a part month, so the status on the day before the wage period decides the whole month, here and at 60. A domestic servant is not an employee unless the employee gave one month's notice to be a member (paras (2)-(3)). A student on industrial training engaged without a contract of service or apprenticeship is not an employee (s.2).

references.title: Employees Provident Fund (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act A1760)

name: Employees Provident Fund (permanent residents aged 60 and above)

references.title: Employees Provident Fund Act 1991 (Act 452)
references.locator: s.43 and Third Schedule Part C
references.quote: A permanent resident, or a non-citizen who elected to contribute before 1 August 1998, who has attained 60: employee 5.5% of wages, employer 6.5% for wages up to RM5,000 a month and 6% above that, and 5.5% / 6% for the months where wages exceed RM20,000. The printed ladder repeats Part A's brackets (RM10 to RM20, RM20 to RM5,000, RM100 to RM20,000) with the contribution taken on the band's upper limit and rounded up to the next ringgit. Above the table the total contribution is rounded up to the next ringgit and the employer’s share is that total less the employee’s rounded share, never two separate round-ups. Part C note: a bonus that lifts a monthly wage of RM5,000 or below over RM5,000 keeps the employer at 6.5% of the month’s wages, the total rounded to the next ringgit. Part A para 1(c) and Part C para 1(c): a non-citizen who elected to contribute before 1 August 1998 stays on Part A below 60 and Part C from 60; the same bonus note covers them. Above RM20,000 each share is the exact percentage of the wage and only the total, with its cents, is rounded up to the next ringgit.

references.title: Employees Provident Fund (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act A1760)
references.quote: Part F: a non-citizen employee and the employer each contribute 2% of the wages, in operation 1 October 2025 (P.U.(B) 354/2025), mandatory from October 2025 wages (November 2025 contribution month). Charged on the wage as it stands: no Third Schedule bracketing and no wage ceiling. Para 2: “The total contribution which includes cents shall be rounded to the next ringgit”. It does not say which share carries the rounding; read here as the two 2% shares totalled and rounded up once, the employee share exact to the sen and the employer the rounded total less it (RM1,751: 35.02 + 35.02 = 70.04 → RM71; employee 35.02, employer 35.98). Prints no age because the exclusion sits in the First Schedule.

name: Non-Employment Injury Security Scheme (LINDUNG 24 Jam)

references.title: Employees’ Social Security (Amendment) Act 2026 (Act A1788)
references.locator: s.3 (Act 4 s.6(4)-(5), (11)); s.17, Third Schedule column (4)(B) "Non-employment injury"
references.quote: In operation 1 June 2026. First-category contributions by Part I, II or III and second-category by Part IV, V or VI of the Third Schedule for the First, Second and Third Phase; employee share only; the second-category column (4) is the same amount in every band. Introduces the Skim Kemalangan Bukan Bencana Kerja (LINDUNG 24 Jam) under Act 4. Wages to RM200 are the printed amounts; Phase I = round(1.25% × band midpoint, 5 sen, half to even) − 0.5% × midpoint (RM200.01–300 → RM1.85), Phase II = 1.00% × midpoint, Phase III = round(1.25% × midpoint, 5 sen, half to even). Employee share only, 0.75% of wages in Phase 1 (years 1-2 from 1 June 2026), rising to 1.00% in Phase 2 (years 3-5) and 1.25% in Phase 3 (year 6 onwards). Charged in both the First and the Second Category on the same wage bands and the same RM6,000 ceiling as SOCSO. The 65 rows are A1788 Third Schedule Part I column (4)(B) (Part IV column (4) for the Second Category, identical in every band). A six-month grace period from 1 June 2026 runs before penalties. The Second and Third Phase amounts (Parts II/V and III/VI) apply from 1 June 2028 and 1 June 2031. PERKESO’s consolidated Act 4 text (as at 1 September 2022) predates A1724/2024 and A1788 and is not the source of these amounts.

references.title: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53), Schedule 6
references.quote: AGC online text as at 1 January 2026. Para 15(1)(b): compensation for loss of employment exempt up to RM10,000 a completed year of service. Para 25C: long service award exempt up to RM2,000 per employee per year of assessment only after more than ten years with the same employer. Para 21(a): a non-resident employed in Malaysia for no more than 60 days in the year is exempt; para 22(a): past 60 days the exempted months are recovered. Para 13: official travelling allowance up to RM6,000 a year and child care allowance up to RM3,000; past-achievement / service-excellence / long-service awards up to RM2,000 together; none for an employee who controls the employer.

references.title: LHDN, Specification for Monthly Tax Deduction (MTD) 2026
references.locator: sections D and E; D(a) note p.9; D(2) Steps 1(C/E) and 4; D(3)-(5); E(9) item v p.21; E(5), E(13), E(15)
references.quote: Assessment years outside 2026 require further verification. Resident: year-to-date formula P = Σ(Y − K*) + (Y1 − K1) + (Y2 − K2)n + (Yt − Kt) − (D + S + DU + SU + QC); all EPF relief within RM4,000. D RM9,000 (the only automatic relief, D.2(i) item a); S RM4,000 spouse without income; DU RM7,000 disabled individual; SU a further RM6,000 disabled spouse; QC child relief RM2,000 under 18 or studying, RM8,000 tertiary or disabled, RM16,000 disabled in tertiary education, half amounts for a shared child. Normal MTD = [tax − (Z + X)] ÷ (n + 1), truncated to the sen and rounded up to 5 sen; additional remuneration adds the year’s tax with Yt − Kt; each component under RM10 is not deducted; the month’s zakat is then rebated. Optional deductions item k (D.2(ii)): SOCSO/EIS RM350 a year, the specification’s worked examples carry LP1 = 0 on a RM5,500 wage. D(a): exempt income is excluded from MTD remuneration; "With effect from August 2017, MTD for resident on foreign workers is applicable to employees with an employment contract of or more than 182 days". Non-resident 30%. D(b) and E(13): current additional-remuneration EPF is included once in the additional-pay calculation. D(3)-(5): approved REP, knowledge-worker and relocation C-suite profiles are 15% of projected chargeable income after relief and accumulated PCB/rebates; REP and knowledge-worker profiles retain the RM400/RM800 low-chargeable-income rebate, C-suite none; REP requires Malaysian citizenship, C-suite non-citizenship; REP and C-suite periods are exactly five consecutive assessment years. E(5), E(15): external zakat and religious-travel departure levy are rebates in the accepted claim month; full rebate amounts remain in history even when current PCB is zero. Accumulated MTD excludes CP38 directed instalments; accumulated rebates retain the full qualifying zakat, including TP3 openings. E(9): exempt perquisites leave the MTD remuneration (official travelling allowance up to RM6,000 a year, child care allowance up to RM3,000, awards up to RM2,000 together).

references.locator: paras 1-2 (normal and additional remuneration): P, K, K1, K2, Kt, n and n + 1; Steps 1-5; Table 1
references.quote: MTD = [(P - M) R + B - (Z + X)] / (n + 1), where P = [sum(Y - K) + (Y1 - K1) + (Y2 - K2) n + (Yt - Kt)] - [D + S + DU + SU + QC + (sum LP + LP1)]. The additional-remuneration method computes the same P with the current month's (Yt - Kt) and withholds the difference between the total tax for the year and X + the normal MTD for the month x (n + 1). Rounding: cut to sen, then up to the next 5 sen; below RM10 no deduction.

references.title: Encoded 2026-11-04: actual year-to-date and a bonus paid once
references.quote: sum(Y - K) and X come from this employee's ctx.balances for the tax year: ytd.FINAL_PAY less the year's exempt pay, and statutory_contribution for the EPF, SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK and PCB employee shares, never from a contract rate or a whole-year multiplication of the current month. Y1 is ORDINARY_WAGES less exempt pay, arrears, commission not paid monthly and awards, plus official travel above its limit. Yt is the bonus, arrears, commission not paid monthly, taxable awards and compensation, and final settlements, so one-off pay enters P once; Y2 repeats only Y1. K1 is the declared pcb_epf_normal_month when supplied, otherwise the employee EPF apportioned by EPF wages. In a bonus-only run Y1 is zero, so Y2 is zero and the next normal run catches up through X. Payroll zakat is the ZAKAT checkpoint: the month's nets off Step 1[D], earlier months' are in Z (E(5)).

references.title: Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001 (Act 612)

Registration is compulsory at 10 or more Malaysian employees and the levy is 1% of monthly wages; at 5 to 9 Malaysian employees registration is optional and the 0.5% levy falls due only once the employer has elected to register. s.2: the levy and the headcount test are on Malaysian citizens; a permanent resident is not a Malaysian employee. ss.2, 14-15 exclude domestic servants and part-time wages; the mandatory employer levy remains due without registration while the optional class needs an election. s.2 "wages" (AGC reprint 2017) "includes any leave pay"; it does not list payment for untaken leave among the exclusions (a)-(f) and it is not the (d) gratuity on discharge, so payment for untaken annual leave under Employment Act 1955 s.60E(3A) is levy wages.
